title: M7 Retire Amplify reader apps and reader template resources
description:
## Outcome
No Markus site uses an Amplify reader app; the template no longer creates reader apps for markus-static, which relieves apps-per-account pressure (6 of 30 apps today -> 4; one app per future Markus site instead of two).

## Design
/Users/home/Projects/markus-publication-architecture-v2.md section 5 (Default publication option: what gets removed).

## Checklist
- [ ] Template: remove markus-static reader app resources, reader build specs, custom rules, amplify:StartJob/ListJobs grants, PAPYRUS_READER_AMPLIFY_APP_ID wiring
- [ ] Retire the CMS staging full build for Markus sites if previewItem replaces it (decision)
- [ ] Update docs/site-hosting.md hosting axis ("s3-projection" replaces amplify-static for Markus)
- [ ] List retired resources for Ryan (he deletes them)

## Acceptance
- Synth snapshot of a markus fixture site: zero AWS::Amplify::App for the reader; pretext sites unchanged.
- aws amplify list-apps in papyrus-production shows no *-reader apps after Ryan's deletions.

## Out of scope
Deleting resources (Ryan does it).

## Dependencies
Blocked by M6.

## Risk
Low.

## Estimate
2-3 agent-hours.

comments.text: home (claude_code / claude-sonnet-5-5): M7 evidence. Papyrus PR #199 merged (c38223b), release 1.0.0-next.49. (1) Markus brands without backend.reader now default to publication {kind: s3-projection, reprojectOnDeploy: true}; opt out with publication:false; an explicit publication object is used as written (default-publication.ts). (2) App-shell: reader is optional for markus-static with a cms section; new cms.stagingPreview {buildCommand, baseDirectory} keeps the staging draft-preview build (moving reader.buildCommand/baseDirectory there gives a byte-identical staging build spec); decision on the checklist item: the staging full build is NOT retired (no previewItem exists). Synth test: Pilobol fixture without reader has 1 Amplify app, no Reader outputs or ReaderServiceRole. (3) reprojectOnDeploy: a custom resource in stack reproject-on-deploy invokes content-actions async with projectionTask all on every backend deploy (new task in handler.run_projection_task, Lambda timeout 300 s only when enabled); explicit publication objects stay off unless set, so Pilobol/Anth do not change. (4) 404 headers: the viewer-response function in the edge template drops cache-control for non-200 and strips the charset, so no writer change was needed. (5) infra/edge/ now holds pilobol-us.yaml, anth-us.yaml, anth-us-s3.yaml and a README with the ACM DNS-validation notes (answer to Q4: distribution.create + acm or certificateArn already existed from M1). Template-diff proof: app-shell templates synthesized from Pilobol.us, Anth.us, p.apyr.us, Threat-Intelligence (site.json as committed on main) and the Pretext example are byte-identical between develop and this change; Pilobol next.29 vs next.49 and Anth next.41 vs next.49 are identical too. Evidence /Users/home/Projects/.baselines/m7-20261013/. Site PRs, not merged: AnthusAI/Pilobol.us#67, AnthusAI/Anth.us-Papyrus#30 (bodies say loudly that deploying deletes the reader app). Unexecuted diffs (computed from synthesized templates because the AWS SSO session was expired): destroy ReaderServiceRole, its policy, ReaderApp, ReaderBranch (+ReaderDomain for Pilobol), outputs ReaderAppId/ReaderOrigin; narrows the authoring and CI role policies; nothing else. RISK for Ryan: Pilobol's ReaderDomain (pilobol.us Amplify domain association) is deleted by the deploy; the runbook pre-check verifies DNS does not depend on it. Runbook: /Users/home/Projects/m7-retirement-runbook.md. Status left for Ryan.

right_now_summary: The template no longer creates reader apps, and Ryan must delete the existing resources.
